name: B — Sweet Spot (the build I would actually buy for modded Minecraft on Bazzite)
target: All the Mods / 200+ mod packs with Iris shaders at 1440p, 32 chunks + Distant Horizons

cpu.name: AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D
cpu.why: Same CPU as the flagship. Do not downgrade this — in modded Minecraft it is worth more than the next GPU tier up.

cooler.name: Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE V2
cooler.why: A 120 W, single-CCD X3D chip does not need liquid. This $35 cooler holds ~85-90 C under all-core load and is silent in game loads; only buy the 360 AIO if you want lower fan noise at 100% sustained rendering.

motherboard.name: Gigabyte B850 Eagle WiFi 6E
motherboard.why: PCIe 5.0 x16 and a PCIe 5.0 M.2 for ~$190. A 9850X3D does not need an X870 board; the money is better spent on RAM or a second SSD.

memory.name: 32 GB (2x16 GB) DDR5-6000 CL30 EXPO
memory.why: 32 GB is the honest floor for 200+ mod packs on Linux (12 GB heap leaves ~19 GB for Bazzite, browser and shader compiler). This is the compromise part of the build: DDR5 is up ~470% from its low, so 64 GB adds ~$570 for headroom you may not need.

gpu.name: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB
gpu.why: Same card as the flagship — it is the price/performance peak for Minecraft shaders in this market.

storage.name: WD_BLACK SN850X 2 TB NVMe
storage.why: DRAM-cached Gen4, mature Linux support, no firmware drama. Gen5 buys nothing for Minecraft.

psu.name: MSI MPG A1000GS 1000 W (ATX 3.1, 80+ Gold)
psu.why: It is currently cheaper than most 750 W units and gives headroom for a future high-TDP GPU.

case.name: Lian Li Lancool 207
case.why: Best-in-test thermals for ~$80; two 140 mm front + two 120 mm bottom fans included. Zero software needed.

monitor.name: Gigabyte MO27Q2A 27" 1440p 240 Hz OLED
monitor.why: Cheapest good 1440p 240 Hz OLED in Nov 2026; shaders + HDR on Bazzite look excellent here.
